planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container on a moss pole or trellis in bright, indirect light in well-drained, chunky, humus-rich potting mix; Florida Beauty philodendron holds its cream-and-green variegation best with consistent bright indirect light.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container on a moss pole or trellis in bright, indirect light in well-drained, chunky, humus-rich potting mix; Florida Beauty philodendron holds its cream-and-green variegation best with consistent bright indirect light. Deeply lobed, uniquely shaped leaves are heavily splashed and speckled in cream, yellow, and pale green over a darker green base, no two leaves patterned quite alike, on a climbing hybrid vine believed to descend from Philodendron pedatum crossed with a variegated relative. Its unusual, deeply cut leaf shape combined with bold, splashy variegation makes it a sought-after specimen for collectors, and it climbs readily up a moss pole to produce larger, more dramatically lobed and patterned leaves as it matures. Prune out any leaves that revert to solid green to keep the plant's energy focused on variegated growth, and rotate the pot for even light exposure.
sources: American Society for Horticultural Science reference

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant, hanging basket, or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained potting mix; Rio philodendron is an easy, fast-growing variegated selection tolerant of average indoor conditions.

directions: Grow as a houseplant, hanging basket, or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained potting mix; Rio philodendron is an easy, fast-growing variegated selection tolerant of average indoor conditions. A variegated form of heartleaf philodendron, it produces narrow, distinctively wave-edged and lobed leaves streaked in shades of yellow, cream, and light green over darker green, giving the trailing vine a more sculptural, textured look than the plain heartleaf or the broader-striped 'Brasil' cultivar. It roots easily from stem cuttings, grows quickly under average indoor light, and trails attractively from a hanging basket or shelf, making it a forgiving, low-maintenance choice for gardeners newer to variegated aroids. Pinch trailing stems to encourage bushier growth and provide bright indirect light to keep the variegation crisp.
sources: American Society for Horticultural Science reference

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained, chunky, humus-rich potting mix; Imperial Red philodendron is a compact, self-heading (non-climbing) selection that needs no moss pole or trellis.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained, chunky, humus-rich potting mix; Imperial Red philodendron is a compact, self-heading (non-climbing) selection that needs no moss pole or trellis. Large, broad, glossy leaves emerge deep burgundy-red and mature to a rich dark green with red-tinged petioles and undersides, forming a dense, upright rosette rather than a climbing vine, unlike its close relative 'Red Emerald.' Its bold, compact, non-vining habit and large leaf size make it a striking floor specimen for a shaded corner without the need for staking or vertical support, and it tolerates lower indoor light better than many other bold-foliage aroids. Wipe dust from the large glossy leaves periodically and water when the top inch of potting mix has dried.
sources: American Society for Horticultural Science reference

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded, humid patio container in bright, indirect light in a loose, well-drained, chunky epiphytic mix; Pink Champion anthurium wants consistent warmth and humidity and blooms best with steady bright indirect light.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded, humid patio container in bright, indirect light in a loose, well-drained, chunky epiphytic mix; Pink Champion anthurium wants consistent warmth and humidity and blooms best with steady bright indirect light. Glossy, heart-shaped, deep green leaves set off long-lasting, waxy, bright pink spathes surrounding a pale, contrasting spadix, produced nearly year-round under good indoor conditions and prized as long-stemmed cut flowers as well as a flowering houseplant. Like other flamingo-flower anthuriums it is an epiphyte in habitat and performs best in a loose, chunky, orchid-bark-based mix that drains quickly rather than a dense potting soil that holds excess moisture around the roots. Feed lightly during the growing season to sustain repeat bloom, keep humidity above 50 percent where possible, and remove spent spathes at the base to tidy the plant.
sources: American Society for Horticultural Science reference

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant, hanging basket, or shaded patio container in low to bright indirect light in well-drained potting mix; Jade pothos is among the most shade-tolerant and forgiving houseplants, thriving in lower light than variegated pothos cultivars.

directions: Grow as a houseplant, hanging basket, or shaded patio container in low to bright indirect light in well-drained potting mix; Jade pothos is among the most shade-tolerant and forgiving houseplants, thriving in lower light than variegated pothos cultivars. Solid, glossy, deep emerald-green heart-shaped leaves cover fast-growing trailing stems with no variegation to fade or revert, making this the simplest, most reliably vigorous pothos to grow in the dim corners, hallways, and low-light offices where fancier variegated cultivars often struggle and lose their pattern. It roots readily from stem cuttings in water or soil, tolerates irregular watering, and is a common choice for beginners and for propagating quickly to fill hanging baskets or line a shelf. Let the potting mix dry between waterings and trim leggy stems periodically to keep the plant full and bushy.
sources: American Society for Horticultural Science reference

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging basket, or mount on a slab, in bright, indirect light in a loose, fast-draining, chunky potting mix; Curtis's hoya is a small, slow-growing miniature best suited to a small pot, terrarium, or mounted display.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging basket, or mount on a slab, in bright, indirect light in a loose, fast-draining, chunky potting mix; Curtis's hoya is a small, slow-growing miniature best suited to a small pot, terrarium, or mounted display. Tiny, thick, silver-speckled, heart-shaped leaves lie closely along thin, wiry, creeping stems that root as they spread, forming a dense, low mat or a delicate curtain when allowed to trail from a small hanging pot. Native to Southeast Asian forests, it is among the smallest and slowest-growing hoya species commonly cultivated, making it well suited to windowsill, terrarium, or miniature garden displays where larger hoyas would be out of scale. Let the potting mix dry between waterings, provide bright filtered light for the best leaf speckling, and avoid overpotting this slow-growing miniature in too large a container.
sources: American Society for Horticultural Science reference

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in fast-draining, chunky potting mix; Shooting Star hoya has a more upright, shrubby habit than most trailing hoya species and benefits from light staking when young.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in fast-draining, chunky potting mix; Shooting Star hoya has a more upright, shrubby habit than most trailing hoya species and benefits from light staking when young. Glossy, lance-shaped leaves clothe a semi-upright, shrubby plant that produces dramatic, dense clusters of dozens of small, narrow, swept-back yellow-to-white flowers with reflexed petals, resembling a burst of tiny shooting stars and giving the plant its common name. Native to Southeast Asian forests, it blooms more readily and at a younger age than many hoya species, and its shrubbier, less vining habit makes it a good choice for a floor or tabletop specimen rather than a hanging basket. Provide bright indirect light for reliable flowering, let the potting mix dry between waterings, and never remove the woody flowering spurs, which rebloom for years.
sources: American Society for Horticultural Science reference

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained, chunky potting mix; Rosso peperomia stores water in its thick leaves and prefers to dry out somewhat between waterings, like other ripple peperomias.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained, chunky potting mix; Rosso peperomia stores water in its thick leaves and prefers to dry out somewhat between waterings, like other ripple peperomias. Deeply quilted, ruffled, dark green leaves with a metallic sheen are strikingly backed in solid burgundy-red, an eye-catching two-tone effect visible whenever a leaf turns or catches the light, set off by slender, upright, mouse-tail-like flower spikes above the compact rosette. Its naturally tidy, symmetrical growth habit needs little pruning or shaping, and the plant's small scale suits a windowsill, desk, or terrarium as well as a mixed dish garden. Water only when the top inch of potting mix has dried, and propagate easily from leaf cuttings rooted in moist soil.
sources: American Society for Horticultural Science reference
